1. 에베소서 기록 목적\n 1) 바울이 로마에서 기록한 옥중서신, 특히:
1. Why Ephesians was written
 1) Among the Prison Epistles Paul wrote in Rome, Ephesians and Colossians in particular were written when Paul's theology had come to full maturity.
 - Before, whenever a church had a problem, he'd send a letter to sort the problem out, right? His emotions would show in those letters too. But now the apostle Paul is past 60, so his character has become much gentler and humbler. So the mood is a bit different from 1 & 2 Corinthians or Galatians.
 2) A change in the apostle Paul's view of the world and of history
 - It's not that a problem came up in the Ephesian church; it's that something big changed in Paul's heart. Back on his first and second missionary journeys, Paul thought Jesus was coming very soon, you know? The Holy Spirit came down just a week after Jesus ascended, so he thought the Second Coming would come just as quickly, and then he realized it wasn't so.
 - Even in Romans you can see that the Second Coming isn't treated as a major theme anymore. After bringing the gospel to Rome, he planned to go all the way to Spain if the Roman church would support him, because people back then thought Spain was the ends of the earth. He thought, once the gospel reaches the ends of the earth, won't Jesus come? But when he got to Rome he saw that it doesn't end if you go west; there are huge numbers of nations and peoples to the north too, so he realized the gospel hadn't yet reached everyone.
 - And with that, he came to know that the world wasn't the small world he had thought, and so that Jesus wasn't going to come back that quickly. He came to know it through knowledge, through information, through common sense, and through revelation.
 3) - So then he came to think: we can't run the church this loosely; we have to systematize it, organize it, and build it up solid. Up to now he'd been concerned only with personal salvation, being justified by faith, but now he came to think he needed to build a solid church made up of those saved people. So the theme of Ephesians is ecclesiology. The theory of the church. Ecclesiology
<엡1:1~2> 하나님의 뜻으로 말미암아 그리스도 예수의 사도 된 바울은: <Eph 1:1~2> Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus: Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

3. Every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places
 1) Every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places
<엡1:3> 찬송하리로다 하나님 곧 우리 주 예수 그리스도의 아버지께서:
<Eph 1:3> Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ:
 - He praises God because God gives every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.
택함, 예정, 양자됨, 구속(죄사함), 비밀을 알리심. 믿게해서 백성 삼: Chosen, predestined, adopted as sons, redeemed (sins forgiven), the mystery made known. He made us believe and made us His people.
☞ 정리하자면 창세 전에 그리스도 안에서 우리를 택하시고, 그 기쁘신 뜻: ☞ To sum up: before the foundation of the world He chose us in Christ, predestined us according to His good pleasure, made us His sons through Jesus Christ, gave us redemption and the forgiveness of sins through that Son, made it overflow with wisdom and understanding, made known to us the mystery of His will, and sealed us with the Holy Spirit, setting us apart forever as His people and His children. The gathering of people who have received this grace and blessing is the church. That church is the body of Christ, united with Christ. So because it is one Spirit, because it is one body, one life comes in. He's talking about a concept bigger than the universe.
<엡1:14> 이는 우리의 기업에 보증이 되사 그 얻으신 것을 구속하시고:
<Eph 1:14> Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.
 - We came into this world for nothing else but exactly this. Once he realized this, whether he was locked up or not, he burst out, "Blessed be God!"
4. 1장의 나머지 내용 - 바울의 기도: 4. The rest of chapter 1 - Paul's prayer
5. 2장의 내용\n- 허물과 죄로 죽었던 너희를 살리셨다. 죽을 수 밖:
5. What chapter 2 says
- You who were dead in trespasses and sins, He made alive. Not "bound to die," but "dead." Already dead. And He reconciled us like that to God, through the cross... Before, you had no circumcision, you were nothing but outsiders to the covenants of promise, you had no hope and no God, but now through the blood Christ shed you have been brought near to God.
- So now you have become fellow heirs, fellow citizens, and members of God's household. Verse 22: and so you are becoming a dwelling place for God, and that's exactly the church.
<엡3:1~4> 이러므로 그리스도 예수의 일로 너희 이방을 위하여 갇힌:
<Eph 3:1~4> For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles, If ye have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me to you-ward: How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ)
 -In the original there's no "I say" (말하거니와, as the Korean Bible has it); there's a "...". Paul, who knew this mystery, was so moved he couldn't go on, so Tertius, who was writing it down, put a "...". Someone later added "I say."
That mystery is something that wasn't even revealed to the Old Testament prophets; it's verse 6. That the Gentiles too, through the gospel, become fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise.
- Then Paul's prayer continues: he asks that they be strengthened in the inner man, that Christ dwell in their hearts, that they know the love of Christ, and that they be filled with all the fullness of God.
7. 4장의 내용\n - 우리가 예정을 입어서 그리스도의 몸 된 교회에:
7. What chapter 4 says
 - If we are predestined and have a part in the church, the body of Christ, how should we live? That practical part starts from chapter 4.
 - With humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, keep the unity the Spirit has given.
- Don't live like the Gentiles do. Throw off debauchery, greed, impurity... and become a new man.
 - Two things to notice => Don't grieve the Holy Spirit
Forgive one another, just as God in Christ forgave you.
이런 덕목들이 바로 교회를 든든하게 하는 것들이기 때문에 바울이 강조하는: Virtues like these are exactly what make the church solid, and that's why Paul stresses them.
<엡5:1> 그러므로 사랑을 입은 자녀같이 너희는 하나님을 본받는 자가:
<Eph 5:1> Be therefore imitators of God, as beloved children.
 - The level Paul asks of us goes all the way to "imitators of God." So even if we've reached a certain level, there's no "This much is good enough." The goal is to become like Jesus. How far? To abide in love the way Christ loved.
 - And he tells us to bear the fruit of light, and the fruit of light, simply put, is being good, righteous, and true.  Then he gives instructions to husbands and wives, and first comes the verse wives love, right?
아내=>복종 - 교회가 그리스도에게 복종한 것처럼: Wife => submit - just as the church submitted to Christ
남편=>사랑 - 그리스도께서 교회를 사랑하신 것처럼, 그 교회를 위해서: Husband => love - just as Christ loved the church, just as He gave Himself for the church
아내들은 복종이란 말 싫어합니다. 그런데 복종과 사랑 중에 어느게 더 어: Wives hate the word "submit." But which is harder, submitting or loving? If wives submit, husbands love just as Christ gave Himself for the church, that is, they love by laying down their lives.
다시...복종하는 것과 목숨을 바치는 것 어떤게 쉽습니까?: Again... submitting or laying down your life, which is easier?
이건 누가 먼저랄것 없이 동시에 해야 합니다. 먼저 복종해! 사랑해 줄게: Nobody goes first here; you have to do it at the same time. "You submit first! Then I'll love you." "Try loving me a little! Then I'll gladly submit!" That doesn't work. At the same time...
왜 이렇게 해야 하느냐? 27절 거룩하고 흠이 없게 하시려고, 반대로 말: Why do it this way? Verse 27: to make it holy and without blemish. Put the other way, if the wife doesn't submit and the husband doesn't love, the church isn't holy.
바울은 남편과 아내가 각각 해야 할 일을 말했는데 저는 반대로 한 마디: Paul told husbands and wives what each should do, but I'd like to add a word going the other way. Ladies only, listen up. Act lovable toward your husbands. That's submission.
남자들 잘 들어요. 아내가 복종할 만큼 훌륭한 남편이 되십시오. 아내를: Men, listen up. Be a husband good enough that your wife will submit. Die for your wife. Just do it.
9. What chapter 6 says
 - Here's the verse parents love.
<엡6:1~3> 자녀들아 너희 부모를 주 안에서 순종하라 이것이 옳으니라:
<Eph 6:1~3> Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
- Kids these days seem to say, "Just convince me with logic and then I'll obey..." But God's word is firm. Obey. This is right. But it's obeying in the Lord. The parents have to be in the Lord first, so that the children can obey in the Lord, right?
- It says if you honor your parents you'll live long on the earth, and I used to not understand how honoring parents and living long were connected. But I came to understand it through the lectures. God sees a person who honors those who brought him into existence as worth keeping in existence. And beyond honoring your parents, if at the root you honor God who created us, you don't just live long, you live forever. Eternal life.
여러분 이 땅에서 좀 더 잘 살려고 아등바등 하지 마세요. 이 땅에서 잘: Don't scramble so hard to live a bit better on this earth. The secret to doing well on this earth isn't getting into Seoul National University and landing a job at a good company; it's honoring your parents. Paul says this is the first commandment with a promise. Instead of spending your time building up a great résumé, spend it honoring your parents. This is God's promise. Give it a try.
<엡6:4> 또 아비들아 너희 자녀를 노엽게 하지 말고 오직 주의 교양과:
<Eph 6:4> And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
 - When do you get angriest at your parents? When you get scolded unfairly, when they won't let you do what you want,
 - Next, the basic virtues to keep between servants and masters
상전 - 위협 X, 너에게도 상전이 계시다. 그 분은 외모로 사람을 보지: Master - no threatening X, you have a Master too. He does not judge people by appearance. No status X
<엡6:10~13> 종말로 너희가 주 안에서와 그 힘의 능력으로 강건하여:
<Eph 6:10~13> Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
- After you've had a fight, think about it quietly. Our fight really isn't against flesh and blood. In the end you go, "Ah, I fell for the devil's trick again." Fighting people is maybe no big deal. Fighting the devil you can't even see, that's the real fight. From verse 14 he uses a fully armed soldier as the example: the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, the shoes of the gospel, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. The only weapon for attack is the Word. Jesus too fought the devil with the Word.
바울이 기도 부탁을 하는데 자기가 담대하게 입을 열어 복음을 선포하게 해: Paul asks for prayer, that he could open his mouth boldly and proclaim the gospel...
<엡6:23~24> 아버지 하나님과 주 예수 그리스도에게로부터 평안과 믿:
<Eph 6:23~24> Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace be with all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love.
 - It says grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with unchanging love, but later, when you get to Revelation, this Ephesian church fails to keep loving Jesus unchangingly and loses its first love. So it gets rebuked. We shouldn't be like that, right?
